taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.culm_length_m.note: FEIS's Idaho fescue review (Zouhar 2000, read 2026-10-15): "Culms are erect, from 1 to 3.3 feet (0.3-1 m) tall".

traits.life_span.note: FEIS's Idaho fescue review (Zouhar 2000, read 2026-10-15): "a vigorous, native, long-lived, perennial, cool-season, bunchgrass".

traits.rhizome_habit.note: FEIS's Idaho fescue review (Zouhar 2000, read 2026-10-15): "Plants are strongly caespitose", culms densely tufted in large bunches.

traits.clonal.note: FEIS's Idaho fescue review (Zouhar 2000, read 2026-10-15): "Plants are strongly caespitose": a bunchgrass that spreads by tillers, not runners.

traits.inflorescence.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.florets_per_spikelet.note: Hitchcock (1935) pp. 76-77, no. 33, Festuca idahoensis (bluebunch fescue): "spikelets mostly 5- to 7-flowered"; FEIS (Zouhar 2000) gives 5 to 6.

traits.awns.note: FEIS's Idaho fescue review (Zouhar 2000, read 2026-10-15): "large, awned seeds".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: FEIS's Idaho fescue review (Zouhar 2000, read 2026-10-15): "Leaves are fine, dense, and mostly basal", the tuft "6 to 10 inches (15-25 cm) high"; the blade length stated here is the tuft's height.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as FEIS calls the leaves only fine (Zouhar 2000).

traits.flowering_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as the FEIS review read gives no months.

generator.params.note: Roemer's fescue's values, its close relative, with a denser tuft (FEIS, Zouhar 2000: "strongly caespitose", "Leaves are fine, dense, and mostly basal"). The culm height comes from the stated culm length by the rule. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 60 cm at 4 years, within FEIS's 0.3-1 m culms (Zouhar 2000). Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye: blue-green fine leaves, a little bluer than Roemer's fescue's.

traits.awn_length_m.note: Hitchcock (1935) pp. 76-77, no. 33, Festuca idahoensis (bluebunch fescue): lemmas "about 7 mm long; awn usually 2 to 4 mm long".

traits.awn_insertion.note: Hitchcock (1935) p. 57, genus Festuca: lemmas "awned from the tip, or rarely from a minutely bifid apex, sometimes awnless"; for F. idahoensis (pp. 76-77, no. 33) the awn "usually 2 to 4 mm long".

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Hitchcock (1935) pp. 76-77, no. 33, Festuca idahoensis (bluebunch fescue): "panicle narrow, 10 to 20 cm long".

traits.spikelet_length_m.note: Inferred, as no source read gives the spikelet's length: Hitchcock (1935, pp. 76-77) gives lemmas about 7 mm long and spikelets mostly 5 to 7 flowered, and Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, Festuca no. 23) spikelets "about as in F. rubra" (lemmas 5-7 mm, 4-6 flowered); overlapping florets make a spikelet of about 10-14 mm, as Roemer's fescue's 9-13.5 mm.
